strings.name: Haruki Murakami
strings.role: Novelist · Everyday life and other worlds
strings.summary: Murakami began writing while running a jazz bar. His fiction repeatedly explores urban solitude, lost memories and unstable boundaries of reality. Norwegian Wood reached a broad readership, while The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle, Kafka on the Shore and 1Q84 developed layered fictional worlds. He also translates American literature and addressed social trauma in nonfiction such as Underground. The Tale of Kaho appeared in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1949–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Built an international readership through works including Norwegian Wood and Kafka on the Shore, influencing contemporary fiction and translation culture.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Other layers of reality
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle, Kafka on the Shore and 1Q84 weave everyday life into dreams, historical memory and unusual experiences.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Literature across languages
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: His novels circulate internationally. The 2023 Princess of Asturias Award for Literature recognized his writing.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Publishes The Tale of Kaho
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Shinchosha published a novel centered on Kaho, a 26-year-old picture-book creator confronting strange disruptions of everyday life.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Receives the Princess of Asturias literary award
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The Spanish award recognized his writing; The City and Its Uncertain Walls also appeared in Japanese that year.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Begins publishing 1Q84
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The first two volumes introduced intersecting perspectives in a world adjacent to 1984. A third volume followed in 2010.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Publishes Kafka on the Shore
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Parallel journeys of a runaway teenager and an older man connect family fate, music and surreal experience.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Begins The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
strings.timeline.event-05.text: The novel moves from a missing cat and marital crisis toward war memories and violence beneath everyday life.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Publishes Norwegian Wood
strings.timeline.event-06.text: The novel focuses on youthful love, friendship and loss, bringing his work to a much wider readership.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Publishes A Wild Sheep Chase
strings.timeline.event-07.text: The final novel in the early Rat trilogy expanded his quest narratives, blending modern social experience with mystery.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Debuts with Hear the Wind Sing
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Written while he ran a bar, his first novel won the Gunzo new-writer prize and began his career in fiction.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Kyoto
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born in Kyoto and raised near Kobe; later moved to Tokyo to study at Waseda University, encountering drama and Western literature.
